title: Evaluating SAM-based and Convolutional Architectures in Thin Retinal Vessel Segmentation: Model Capacity, Computational Cost and Foundation Pre-training
mechanism: Evidence that a pretrained plain ViT (MedSAM, patch 16) matches the best CNN on thin-vessel centerline recall only when the image is upscaled to its 1024 window; padding loses the thin structures.
adaptation: Fixed rule for every ViT arm: upscale 512 EL to 1024; one ablation inside the SAM2-UNet arm at 512 vs 1024. Explains why our native-resolution probes may have under-read FMs.
min_experiment: SAM2-UNet at 512 vs 1024 input, 5-fold CV; if 1024 is not >= +0.01 crack relF1@2, drop upscaling for all arms.
evidence: R: DRIVE, HRF, FIVES, VessMap; MedSAM thin recall within 0.6 to 2.5 pp of best CNN; padding vs upscaling cut thin recall by 17.9 and 41.3 points; pretraining raised thin recall 17.6 / 12.4 points on two sets.
prior_overlap: Section 5 linear probes ran at native resolution; input upscaling for ViTs not tested (2x input run was on the house CNN).

alt_notes.adaptation: Design rule for every ViT arm here: upscale 512 to 1024, fine-tune (full or PEFT), never frozen probe; report crack recall binned by label width (per source widths 1.5 to 3.25 px).
alt_notes.min_experiment: Within SAM2-UNet or Dino U-Net: 512 vs 1024 input, 3 seeds; metric crack recall on components < 20 px and relF1@2; kill the 1024 arm if gain < 0.012 crack IoU and < 0.01 relF1@2.
